fixed_upstream.relevant_behavior: The fixed upstream uses OneKeyBind openGuiKeybind with default Keyboard.KEY_F and a config.openGui callback; it does not contain the current Minecraft 26.1.2 Fabric KeyMapping client path.

modern_client_boundary.modern_difference: The modern downstream default Right Shift differs from fixed-upstream Keyboard.KEY_F and is undocumented/unreviewed in the fixed upstream. An offhand conflict is a hypothesis only, not a finding.
vanilla_trace: InputConstants.getKey selects SCANCODE when KeyEvent.key() is -1 and KEYSYM otherwise.
KeyboardHandler then calls KeyMapping.set and KeyMapping.click for the resolved InputConstants.Key.
The FarmHelper controller consumes the registered mapping click queue at END_CLIENT_TICK and keeps its existing null-screen guard.

findings.summary: The supplied R4 Shift_R observation does not establish a GLFW or Minecraft KeyEvent identity, so it is not a proven product failure.
findings.upstream_behavior: Fixed upstream opens its GUI from a OneKeyBind whose default is Keyboard.KEY_F and also exposes the shared command callback. The current client is a separate Minecraft 26.1.2 Fabric KeyMapping implementation.

current_master_boundary_reproduction.outcome: The current-master event-to-KeyMapping harness passes a KEYSYM/344 delivery and rejects SCANCODE/54 for a KEYSYM/344 mapping. This proves input identity semantics only; it does not prove which event, if any, the Computer Use Shift_R action delivered to Minecraft.
